# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

14	## Takeaways for the agent
15	
16	1. **Choose terms by C, in code: no lever helps in every case.** The same move flips sign between
17	   cases. Covering 24 months lifted D01 from 0.20 to 0.73 but made P04 dearer. The copper index
18	   clause turned P02's price cut into a score of 0. Before every sheet, score each allowed
19	   combination with `total_cost`, with the supplier's standard terms for unstated fields, and
20	   keep must-haves and C_alt as hard guards.
21	2. **Cover the need where the deal beats the fallback.** Uncovered need costs the fallback price
22	   plus `fallback_risk_pct`. D01 (fallback 55.00, deal 50.90): 24 instead of 12 months, 0.20 to
23	   0.73. P04 (fallback 4.70, price frozen at 4.96): 24 months cost more than 12. P08 (5.72 + 3 %
24	   against 5.93 at 90 days): no difference. P10: 24 months unlocked the full 23,400 units a year
25	   instead of 19,890.
26	3. **Keep every sheet below the supplier's price until the price is right.** 15 of the 16 practice
27	   threads that reached `agreed` never moved price again ("Our agreed offer stands"). The one
28	   exception (P02) gave 0.7 % for 14-day payment. An instant `agreed` means we offered too much:
29	   Dralveck took our opening sheet in round 1 in both P05 runs. In P10 our own sheet raised an
30	   agreed 32.00 to 32.45.
31	4. **The floors sit far below where we stopped.** Expressed as a unit price at our deal's terms,
32	   C_best lies 7 to 22 % below our deal price in six cases: P05 -22 %, P18 -21 %, P10 -16 %,
33	   P08 -14 %, P07 -11 %, P11 -7 %. Tacto's house agent scored 0.74 on P02 and 0.75 on P08, where
34	   we got 0 and 0.11. Our probe offered the supplier's own price from round 2, so it never
35	   measured how far prices fall. That is the open experiment.
36	5. **Trade payment days at the supplier's rate against our 8 %.** Suppliers price 60 more days at
37	   their own cost of money (table under Supplier behaviour). Take the longest payment where that
38	   rate is below 8 %: P03 at +0.7 % for 90 days scores 0.68 instead of our 0.60. Pay faster only
39	   for a supplier that values cash far above 8 %. Every 30 days earlier than the reference 60
40	   costs us 0.67 % of spend.
41	6. **Refuse index clauses on series the case expects to rise.** A clause adds `material_share`
42	   times (expected move beyond the deadband + `index_risk_pct`) of spend. P02 (copper
43	   +5 %, risk 4 %, share 0.2): the clause costs 1.8 % of spend, Nordmark gave 1.5 % for it
44	   (374.32 to 368.70) and the deal scored 0. Its no-clause offer scores 0.21, the same clause
45	   with a 5 % deadband 0.55 (both before the relationship charge). P08 and P18 (AS-14404 +6 %,
46	   risk 1 %, share 0.45): the offered Preisgleitklausel costs 3.2 % of spend.
47	7. **Use the structural levers: start date, lead time, contract length.** Units bought before
48	   `effective_date` cost the current price. In P01, C_best equals paying about 138.20 (the ask
49	   was 138.55) with an April start and 90-day payment. We got 133.60 with a November start and
50	   14 days (0.64). Late delivery costs a flat `late_cost_per_day` per day: in P05, Hrvelec at 42
51	   days for 33.00 scores 0.30, while we paid its overtime premium for 35 days and scored 0.19.
52	   24-month contracts came free at P03, P04, P07 and P10.
53	8. **Read the supplier before the first move.** The persona traits in notes, quote remarks and
54	   news predicted behaviour. `price_frozen` suppliers never moved price, `cash_need` suppliers
55	   asked for faster payment, `capacity_full` suppliers charged overtime for speed (table under
56	   Persona signals). Every supplier asks "Which volume can you commit to?", also where volume is
57	   fixed: a stock phrase, not a lever.
58	9. **Few claims, exact, and only against the supplier's own drivers.** 44 of 57 claims were
59	   verified, but only one moved price (P01, 1.20). Rising indices are read as support for the
60	   supplier. Write figures without thousands separators. In an RFQ a data ID counts once per
61	   case. No supplier sent a cost breakdown.
62	10. **Words without a sheet move change nothing, and outcomes are deterministic.** Bluff and
63	    urgency on an unchanged sheet left the price unchanged ("My call: hold"). The same moves give
64	    the same numbers, so a practice replay measures our change, and a rule-based supplier
65	    simulator built from the traces is feasible.

91	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The category goal sets the rates of C**, not the case type (P13 is a price
92	  increase under `leverage`, P06 an RFQ under `stabilise`). From all 21 case files:

99	  | `stabilise` | 10 % | yes, sustainable margin 0.5 to 8 % | structure: term, start date, payment, fair clause |

103	  computed with the supplier's true numbers, relationship charge included. D01 walk-away after
104	  one message: c_open 448,810.67, c_best 408,623.99. → One session per case gives its target,

106	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Uncovered need** costs `fallback_unit_price` plus `fallback_risk_pct` % of
107	  it; coverage is `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Committed volume above the need
108	  is bought anyway; months beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn. Evidence and examples:
109	  takeaway 2.

111	  like the case's `index_paths`, plus `index_risk_pct` % of `spend x material_share` whenever a
112	  clause exists. Only a falling path larger than the risk charge makes a clause pay.
113	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Late delivery** is `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`,
114	  one sum per case. Must-haves can cap the lead time (P05: at most 42 days).
115	- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Effective date:** units bought before it cost the current price, so a
116	  later start is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13. D01 at 50.90
117	  and 24 months: April instead of December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87.

119	  days earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.

121	  of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
122	  (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %) unless the supplier's cost floor binds first. It also

327	## Principle
328	
329	Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
330	Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

332	## A case
333	
334	1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
335	   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
336	   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
337	   clamps them.

339	
340	   ```
341	   supplier reply
342	     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
343	     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
344	     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
345	     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
346	     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
347	     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures

350	3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
351	   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.

384	## Supplier estimate
385	
386	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
387	`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:
388	
389	- **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
390	  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
391	- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
392	  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
393	- **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
394	  evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.
395	
396	C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.

398	## Policy

401	at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
402	constants when the stance call times out:
403	
404	| Constant | Values |
405	|---|---|
406	| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
407	| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
408	| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
409	| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
410	| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |
411	
412	Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
413	price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.
414

416	
417	1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
418	2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
419	   fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
420	3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
421	4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
422	5. Persona reading and pacing.
423	6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.
424	
425	## Generalise
426	
427	- Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
428	  case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
429	- Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
430	- Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
431	  missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
432	- Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.
433	
434	## Tactics

436	Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
437	shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
438	before closing.
439	
440	Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
441	effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
442	urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
443	attack on the arena: never.

        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
        self.anchor = None
        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
        self.budget = BUDGET
        self.claims = []
        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | closing | done | ended
        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out

class Negotiator:
    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None):
        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete = case, pkg, complete
        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
        self.sides = {}
        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def setup(self, sid, events):
        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or {}
        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
        s.prof = profile(self.pkg, sid)
        self.sides[sid] = s
        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
            s.state = "ended"
            return s
        part = (case.get("parts") or [None])[0]
        full_cost, own_plant = self.full_cost(part, sid)
        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
        s.est = eco.estimate(case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, self.real_ppm(sid), lead, overtime)
        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            s.budget = 0.3
        if "price_frozen" in signals:
            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
        if "capacity_full" in signals:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
        if "approval_2pct" in signals:
            # bigger steps go to its pricing committee: these suppliers ended early after deep
            # anchors (P02, P07, P10, P18); a mild anchor and small gaps keep them conceding
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.92), min(s.budget, 0.18)
        if near_cost:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
        planned = eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio)
        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.at_price(case, quote, q_price * ratio)
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.quote = round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2)
        if full_cost and not near_cost:
            s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
        s.claims = self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price)
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,
            profile=s.prof,
            full_cost=full_cost,
            near_cost=near_cost,
            terms=s.terms,
            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
            anchor=s.anchor,
            target=s.target,
            budget=s.budget,
            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
        )
        return s

    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
        if own:
            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
        if generic:
            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
        return None, False

    def real_ppm(self, sid):
        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

    # -- reading its reply -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def their_price(self, s, terms):
        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
        if same:
            return terms["unit_price"]
        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

    def switch(self, s, new, why):
        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
        if s.ours:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        if s.theirs:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        s.terms = {**new}
        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})

    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
        """Its reply changed some of our non-price terms (in its counter or an alternative): it told
        us what it values. Take a sheet's terms over when C at its price beats C of our plan at
        our counterpart of that price; when it insists on an index clause, take the clause that
        costs us least."""
        if not s.ours:
            return
        case = self.case
        standing_terms = sheets[0]["terms"]
        clause = standing_terms.get("index_clause")
        if "index_clause" in s.terms and s.terms["index_clause"] != clause and clause:
            # it will not sell this term at a fixed price (raw-material distributors), and it
            # refuses a deadband: we take its clause and keep negotiating the price
            self.switch(s, {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}, "its index clause")
        best_c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing_terms)), s.std, s.est)
        for sheet in sheets:
            terms = sheet["terms"]
            changed = {k: v for k, v in terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in s.terms and s.terms[k] != v}
            changed.pop("index_clause", None)
            if not changed:
                continue
            new = {**s.terms, **changed}
            if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std):
                continue
            if any((k, repr(v)) in s.tried for k, v in changed.items()):
                continue  # we were there before: no flip-flop
            c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, new, terms["unit_price"]), s.std, s.est)
            if c < best_c - max(1.0, 0.001 * best_c):
                best_c = c
                s.tried |= {(k, repr(s.terms.get(k))) for k in changed}
                self.switch(s, new, f"its sheet {changed} costs us less")

    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def move(self, sid, threads):
        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done."""
        case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
        s.prev_state = s.state
        last = latest(events)
        status = last.get("status")
        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
            s.state = "ended"
            return None
        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not sheets:
            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
            return None
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
        if fresh:
            self.adopt(s, sheets)
            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
            s.last_reply = last
        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing", "pushed"):  # we sent its own sheet, our target or a last push
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        if (
            status == "final_offer"
            and os.environ.get("BUYER_PUSH_FINAL")
            and moves_left(case, events) > 0
            and len(self.sides) == 1
        ):
            s.state = "pushed"  # experiment: one more step after its final word
            price = round(max(s.ours[-1] if s.ours else 0, theirs * (1 - float(os.environ["BUYER_PUSH_FINAL"]))), 2)
            return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], self.pick(s, 1, threads), events, theirs)
        if status in DONE or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, moves_left(case, events))
        if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
            s.state = "closing"
            return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, moves_left(case, events))
        price, n_claims, question = self.next_price(s, theirs)
        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
        return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs, question)

    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
        if not s.ours:
            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS, QUESTION
        last = s.ours[-1]
        gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
        share = FRACTION
        if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP:
            share = 0.08  # a deep floor: it moves fast on its own; meeting it now would stop it
        left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
        new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
        if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
            new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
        price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
        price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
        price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS, None

    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
        """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
        less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
        case = self.case
        std = s.std
        c_stand = eco.cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
        alts = [(eco.cost(case, sh["terms"], std, s.est), sh) for sh in sheets[1:]]
        alts = [(c, sh) for c, sh in alts if eco.must_haves_ok(case, sh["terms"], std)]
        if alts and left > 0:
            c, sh = min(alts, key=lambda r: r[0])
            if c < c_stand - 1.0:
                s.state = "mirror"
                terms = {k: v for k, v in sh["terms"].items() if k in case["negotiable"]}
                return self.send(s, [eco.complete_offer(case, terms)], [], events, theirs)
        s.state = "done"
        return None

    def pick(self, s, n, threads):
        """The next unused claims for this supplier: in an RFQ the cheapest rival offer first (a new
        offer is a new argument every round), then its own claims, strongest first."""
        out = []
        rivals = []
        for other, events in threads.items():
            if other == s.sid or latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
                continue
            oid, t = standing(events)
            if oid and t.get("unit_price") and s.theirs:
                price = self.their_price(s, t)
                if price < s.theirs[-1]:
                    rivals.append((price, rival_offer(other, oid, t["unit_price"])))
        pool = [c for _, c in sorted(rivals, key=lambda r: r[0])[:1]] + s.claims
        for c in pool:
            key = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for i in c["ids"]]
            if any(k in self.used for k in key):
                continue
            out.append(c)
            if len(out) >= n:
                break
        return out

    def facts(self, s, sheets, claims, moved):
        """Plain statements the model may use, true by construction."""
        case, out = self.case, []
        fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
        if "volume_per_year" not in case["negotiable"] or fixed.get("volume_per_year"):
            out.append("our order volume is fixed: it is our full demand for this part over the term, all with them")
        if "payment_days" not in case["negotiable"]:
            out.append("payment terms are fixed for this agreement; we pay reliably on the due date")
        if "contract_months" in case["negotiable"]:
            out.append("we offer a long contract term, which gives them planning security")
        if any(c["kind"] == "forecast" for c in claims) or any(c["kind"] == "forecast" for c in s.claims):
            out.append("our demand forecast for this part is rising")
        if s.ours and len(s.ours) > 1 and s.ours[-1] > s.ours[-2]:
            out.append("our proposal moves toward them again")
        if moved:
            out.append("they moved in their last reply and we appreciate it")
        if claims:
            out.append("the e-mail cites data right after this paragraph (do not repeat it)")
        out.append("the proposal with all terms follows after the data (do not repeat it)")
        return out

    def send(self, s, sheets, claims, events, theirs, question=None):
        first = not s.ours
        moved = len(s.theirs) > 1 and s.theirs[-1] < s.theirs[-2] - 0.005
        price = sheets[0]["unit_price"]
        keys = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]]
        s.pending = {"state": s.prev_state, "keys": keys}
        if s.state not in ("mirror",):
            s.ours.append(price)
            s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
            s.pending["appended"] = True
        tone = "warm" if s.prof.get("warm", True) else "friendly and businesslike"
        asked = len(s.ours) in (1, 3)
        para = llm.paragraph(
            self.complete,
            writer.brief(
                self.case, s.prof, latest(events).get("body"), self.facts(s, sheets, claims, moved), tone, asked
            ),
        )
        body = writer.email(
            self.case, sheets, claims, question, first=first, moved=moved, warm=s.prof.get("warm", True), paragraph=para
        )
        refs = sorted({i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]})
        self.note(s.sid, "send", state=s.state, theirs=theirs, ours=price, claims=[c["kind"] for c in claims])
        subject = latest(events).get("subject") or f"Re: {self.case['title']}"
        if not subject.lower().startswith("re:"):
            subject = f"Re: {subject}"
        return {
            "message": {
                "subject": subject[:300],
                "body": body,
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
                "refs": refs,
            }
        }

    def commit(self, sid):
        """The message reached the supplier: its claims are spent."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        if s.pending:
            self.used.update(s.pending["keys"])
            s.pending = None

    def rollback(self, sid):
        """The message came too late (a timeout): the supplier never read it."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        if s.pending:
            if s.pending.get("appended"):
                s.ours.pop()
                s.gaps.pop()
            s.state = s.pending["state"]
            s.pending = None
            self.note(sid, "rollback")

    # -- close -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def fallback_close(self, threads):
        """(supplier, message) after a failed close: accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps
        the must-haves, else walk away."""
        best = None
        for sid, events in threads.items():
            oid, terms = standing(events)
            std = standard_terms(events) or self.sides[sid].std
            if oid and latest(events).get("status") not in ENDED and eco.must_haves_ok(self.case, terms, std):
                c = eco.cost(self.case, terms, std)
                if best is None or c < best[0]:
                    best = (c, sid, oid)
        if best is None:
            return next(iter(threads)), {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}
        return best[1], {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": best[2]}}

    def best_offer(self, threads):
        """(C, supplier, term_sheet_id) of the cheapest acceptable standing sheet (only a standing
        sheet can be accepted; alternatives were sent back to become standing)."""
        best = None
        for sid, events in threads.items():
            if latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
                continue
            oid, terms = standing(events)
            side = self.sides.get(sid) or Side(sid)
            std = standard_terms(events) or side.std
            if oid and eco.acceptable(self.case, terms, std):
                c = eco.cost(self.case, terms, std, side.est)
                if best is None or c < best[0]:
                    best = (c, sid, oid)
        return best

    def close(self, threads):
        best = self.best_offer(threads)
        if best is None:
            live = [sid for sid, ev in threads.items() if latest(ev).get("status") not in ENDED] or list(threads)
            self.note(None, "walk_away")
            return {"supplier_id": live[0], "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        self.note(best[1], "accept", c=best[0], offer=best[2])
        return {"supplier_id": best[1], "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": best[2]}}}

    def note(self, sid, what, **kw):
        entry = {"t": round(time.time(), 1), "supplier": sid, "what": what, **kw}
        self.notes.append(entry)
        log.info(
            "%s %s %s",
            self.case["case_id"],
            sid,
            {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k not in ("claims", "std", "profile")},
        )


def keepalive_message(events):
    subject = latest(events).get("subject") or "Re: your offer"
    return {"subject": subject[:300], "body": writer.keepalive(), "term_sheets": []}


def deadline_near(deadline, margin=90):
    cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline
    return bool(cap) and time.time() > cap - margin

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: we build an automated BUYER agent that negotiates by e-mail with LLM-driven supplier bots in a procurement hackathon. Each thread has at most 10 messages; the supplier has a hidden cost floor and a patience budget (deep gaps make it send "final_offer" or walk away); it concedes only after we move; once its status is "agreed" its price freezes; behaviour is deterministic. Score = how close our deal's total cost gets to the best deal the supplier would ever accept.

Topic: winning strategies from the Automated Negotiating Agents Competition (ANAC, Genius / NegMAS, 2010-2025) and the bilateral multi-issue negotiation literature (Baarslag, Hindriks, Jonker, Fatima, Faratin/Sierra/Jennings). Cover: time-dependent concession tactics (Boulware vs Conceder, the e parameter), behaviour-dependent (tit-for-tat variants), the BOA framework (bidding, opponent model, acceptance), acceptance conditions (AC_next, AC_time, AC_combi, AC_max) and which performed best, winning agents (e.g. HardHeaded, CUHKAgent, AgentK, Atlas3, PonPokoAgent, AgreeableAgent) and what made them win, handling short deadlines / few rounds.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then a list of 6-10 concrete, implementable rules for a 10-round buyer agent (with numbers where the literature gives them, e.g. Boulware exponents, acceptance thresholds). Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: we build an automated BUYER agent that negotiates price and terms with LLM-driven supplier bots, at most 10 messages per thread. The supplier has a hidden floor price; it typically concedes in shrinking steps (e.g. 52.90, 51.90, 51.40, 51.10, 50.90) and only after we move; behaviour is deterministic. We want to estimate its floor (reservation price) from its concession sequence early, so we know how hard to push and when to stop.

Topic: opponent modelling and reservation-price estimation in automated negotiation. Cover: Bayesian learning of reservation price (Zeng & Sycara 1998), regression / curve fitting of opponent concession curves (Hou 2004, non-linear regression on time-dependent tactics), Gaussian-process prediction of opponent concessions (Williams et al. IAMhaggler), frequency models, Baarslag's survey "Learning about the opponent in automated bilateral negotiation" (2016), and the human-negotiation heuristic that shrinking concessions signal approaching a limit (geometric decay extrapolation). Also: how to detect "concession bait" vs real floor.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, and a concrete algorithm sketch (formulas) to estimate a floor from 2-4 observed counter-offers assuming exponential/geometric or power-law time-dependent concession, with known failure modes. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: we build an automated BUYER agent (code computes numbers, an LLM writes the e-mails) that negotiates against LLM-driven supplier bots (personas with hidden economics, a cost floor, a patience level, roles like sales rep and boss). We want to know what works against LLM counterparts.

Topic: research 2023-2026 on LLM agents negotiating (with each other or humans). Cover: NegotiationArena (Bianchi et al. 2024: e.g. effect of feigning desperation, anchoring, cunning), "How well can LLMs negotiate?" (Davidson et al.), MIT/Vaccaro et al. 2025 large-scale AI negotiation competition ("Advancing AI negotiations" - findings on warmth, dominance, what won), AmazonHistoryPrice / "Measuring bargaining abilities of LLMs" (buyer is harder than seller), ACE / "assistant for negotiation", OG-Narrator (offer generator + LLM narrator split), Meta's CICERO-style planning + language split, and LLM susceptibility to anchoring, sycophancy, politeness, social proof. Legitimate persuasion only; we must NOT prompt-inject (forbidden).

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 800 words: key findings with source URLs and numbers where available, then 6-10 concrete rules for a buyer agent facing LLM supplier personas. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: we are the purchasing team of a German pump maker (fictional), building an automated buyer agent that negotiates with industrial suppliers (foundries, machining shops, seal makers, motor makers, raw-material distributors). Case types: supplier price-increase letters, contract renewals, RFQs with 2-3 bidders, raw-material/index-driven parts, capacity shortages, quality problems (PPM, chargebacks), bundling. Category goals: leverage, routine, quality_first, stabilise, secure_supply. Score is total cost of ownership (price, payment days at 8% interest, freight/Incoterm, lead time, quality, tooling, index clause, uncovered need, a supplier-health charge in strategic categories).

Topic: professional procurement negotiation practice. Cover: Kraljic matrix and how negotiation stance differs per quadrant; how professional buyers answer a supplier price-increase letter (cost-driver decomposition, index-weighted justified increase, notice periods, delaying effective date, splitting the increase); should-cost / cleansheet negotiation; trading payment terms vs price (supplier cost of capital, dynamic discounting, early-payment discounts); index / price-adjustment clauses (deadbands, symmetry, caps, lag); using contract length and volume commitments as currency; dual-sourcing threats and when they are credible; quality chargebacks. Sources: McKinsey, BCG, Kearney, CIPS, ISM, HBR, procurement blogs.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 800 words: key findings with source URLs, then a lever-by-lever playbook (which lever to pull for which supplier situation), 8-12 rules. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent negotiating multi-issue term sheets (unit price, payment days, contract months, volume, start date, lead time, Incoterm, index clause, PPM commitment) with LLM-driven supplier bots. Each message may carry up to 3 alternative term sheets; the supplier picks one and answers it. We score sheets by our own total cost and estimate the supplier's value of each term (its cost of money, overtime for speed, etc.).

Topic: integrative / multi-issue negotiation. Cover: Multiple Equivalent Simultaneous Offers (MESOs; Medvec, Leonardelli, Galinsky, Claussen-Schulz 2005/2006 and later) - effects on outcomes, how many offers, how different they should be, what to learn from the counterpart's choice; logrolling and Pareto efficiency; package vs issue-by-issue negotiation; "nothing agreed until everything agreed"; post-settlement settlements; how to infer the counterpart's issue priorities from their choices/counters (preference elicitation). Also the automated-negotiation view: iso-utility curve bidding (offer different packages of same own utility, choose the one closest to opponent's last bid, e.g. Lai & Sycara, "similarity-based" tradeoff by Faratin, Sierra & Jennings 2002).

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then 6-10 concrete rules for how to build and use the 3 term sheets per message. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent negotiating unit price with LLM-driven supplier bots, max 10 messages per thread. The supplier has a patience budget: an opening too far below its quote makes it send final_offer or walk away; offering at or above its price makes it agree instantly and freeze the price. Practice data: opening 20% below the quote beat 30% below; the best achievable price was typically 7-22% below where we settled.

Topic: experimental negotiation research on first offers, anchoring and concession patterns. Cover: first-offer advantage (Galinsky & Mussweiler 2001), precise vs round anchors (Mason, Lee, Wiley & Ames 2013; Loschelder et al.), the "insult zone" / backfire of extreme anchors (Schweinsberg et al. 2012), justifying offers with reasons, concession size and timing (decreasing concessions signal limits; Hilty & Carnevale "black-hat/white-hat", "door in the face" reciprocity of concessions, Cialdini), number of concessions vs size, the "final offer" credibility, "nibbling", and the effect of first concessions on counterpart satisfaction (Galinsky et al. "winner's curse" of immediate acceptance). 

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with effect sizes and source URLs, then 6-10 concrete rules (with numbers) for opening and conceding over at most 10 rounds. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent in alternating-offer price negotiation with a supplier bot; hard limit of 10 messages per thread and an 8-minute wall clock per case; the supplier has a hidden floor and a hidden patience (cumulative gap budget) after which it issues "final_offer" or walks away. The supplier never concedes without a move from us. Our BATNA is sometimes a fallback price, sometimes nothing.

Topic: game theory and empirical research on bargaining with deadlines and finite rounds. Cover: Rubinstein alternating offers and discounting, finite-horizon bargaining and backward induction, the "deadline effect" (Roth, Murnighan & Schoumaker 1988: agreements cluster at the deadline), Fershtman & Seidmann deadline effect, ultimatum game rejection thresholds (what share of the surplus responders reject), war-of-attrition concession dynamics, bargaining under one-sided incomplete information (screening by the uninformed buyer, Coasean dynamics), and the value of credible commitment (Schelling). What is the optimal strategy for a buyer who does not know the seller's floor and faces a risk of breakdown that rises with how aggressive it is?

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then 5-8 concrete implications (with numbers where possible) for pacing concessions over 10 messages and for when to accept. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent in RFQ cases where 2-3 supplier bots negotiate in parallel threads (each max 10 messages); accepting one ends the case. We may cite a rival's actual standing offer by its data ID (verified by the arena); a fake rival offer is detected and costs trust. Suppliers differ: one is fully booked and charges overtime for speed, one has spare capacity and wants volume, one is cash-short.

Topic: negotiating with multiple competing suppliers. Cover: buyer strategies in multi-bilateral / one-to-many negotiation (e.g. Thomas, Nguyen & Jennings multi-attribute concurrent negotiation, "concurrent negotiation" coordination strategies in automated negotiation, Rahwan's one-to-many negotiation), reverse auction vs negotiation theory (Bulow & Klemperer "auctions versus negotiations" 1996), best-and-final-offer (BAFO) rounds, using competitive pressure without revealing prices (or revealing them: pros/cons), sequencing which supplier to push first, keeping the losing bidder alive as BATNA, how to use non-price differences (lead time, capacity) when comparing bids, and evidence on shopping a quote ("can you beat X?") in procurement practice.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then 6-8 concrete rules for running 2-3 parallel supplier threads to the lowest total cost. Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent whose LLM writes negotiation e-mails to supplier bots (LLM personas: family foundry that remembers how it is treated, corporate group with an approval ladder, cash-short job shop, near-monopolist). Suppliers read tone, questions, arguments, threats, appreciation and urgency; "padding does not buy price"; bluffs and urgency had no effect in our tests; data arguments are fact-checked, and true arguments help only when they hit what the supplier actually cares about.

Topic: what language moves a counterpart in written/e-mail negotiation. Cover: e-negotiation research (Morris et al. 2002 "schmooze or lose", Thompson & Nadler on e-mail negotiation pitfalls), asking diagnostic questions and information exchange (Thompson; "ask about interests"), framing requests as trades ("if you..., then we..."), giving reasons (Langer "because"), fairness framing and objective criteria (Fisher & Ury "Getting to Yes"), Chris Voss tactics (labeling, calibrated questions, accusation audit) and evidence for them, face-saving for the counterpart's boss, effect of expressed anger vs disappointment (Van Kleef), and how to justify a counter-offer with data without sounding adversarial.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then 8-10 concrete writing rules plus 3 short example sentences a buyer e-mail could use (no em-dashes). Flag anything uncertain.

Research task (web research only, do not edit any files). Context: automated BUYER agent for a German pump maker negotiating with industrial suppliers. In "stabilise" and "secure_supply" categories, the score charges us for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (charge grows roughly with the square of the missing points), so the best deal is NOT the lowest price; in "secure_supply" uncovered volume is very expensive (25% risk premium). Some suppliers are cash-short (bank watching, short-time work), some are fully booked and allocate capacity, some have frozen price lists but move on other terms.

Topic: negotiating with strategic, bottleneck, distressed or capacity-constrained suppliers. Cover: supplier distress management (supply chain finance, early payment programs, prepayment, reverse factoring), capacity allocation and being a "customer of choice" (Schiele et al. research on preferred customer status, what suppliers value: volume reliability, forecast visibility, payment reliability, low hassle), cooperative vs competitive procurement negotiation outcomes, handling a supplier that says "price list is frozen, but we can talk about terms", handling an approval ladder (supplier's boss must approve bigger moves), and fair-price arguments (open-book costing, cost-plus with margin).

Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Return under 700 words: key findings with source URLs, then 6-10 concrete rules for which non-price currencies to offer such suppliers and how to secure supply at a fair, sustainable price. Flag anything uncertain.
